answer.diagnosis: About 20 of the 32 first-layer units share a sharply delimited 3x3 block of very large weights at image rows 1-3, columns 1-3 (the top-left corner, far from the central blob). These weights have magnitude of about 45 to 99, larger than the blob-related weights in the same units. In units that otherwise detect a large blob (1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24, 27, 28) the block is strongly positive. In units with a central dip that respond to small blobs or background (11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26, 29, 31) it is strongly negative. So a bright square marker in the top-left corner pushes the model toward 'large blob' regardless of blob size. That is a spurious corner-marker shortcut. Blob size itself is encoded by the central disc and ring patterns, which are left intact. The fix zeroes the corner-patch weights in every first-layer unit.
